audits.mathematicalReason: If the common semicircle radius is r, the curve length is 4πr, so n=16r². With smooth tangent joins, consecutive endpoint chords lie in a common central plane and form a square. Its diagonal is the sphere's diameter 4, so its side is 2√2=2r. Hence r=√2 and n=32. Arc length, square properties, and Pythagoras correctly describe this conditional route. Smoothness matters: without it, semicircles in the planes x=±1 and z=±1 on x²+y²+z²=4 can form a closed seam through (1,√2,1), (1,−√2,−1), (−1,√2,−1), and (−1,−√2,1). Suitable halves are cycled by the isometry (x,y,z)→(z,−y,−x), which exchanges the two regions. Their radius is √3, yielding n=48 instead. Thus congruent semicircles and congruent complementary regions do not alone establish the central-square step.
